steps.name: Sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA, distances)
caveats: Do not use batch-corrected embeddings for QC; the blind VST of the raw counts is the object
Do not drop or down-weight any sample here; flagging only — decisions belong to the user
steps.context: Design: 6 treated vs 6 control; two known processing batches, balanced across conditions. QC must be blind (design-free) so it cannot be driven by the factor of interest. No reference data needed.
steps.question: Do the 12 kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control, 2 balanced processing batches) group by condition, does either batch dominate the leading axes of variation, and does any sample depart from its group — before any test is fitted?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA, sample distances per R-0033@40bf

constraints: Run the blind VST (blind = TRUE) on the raw counts before any modeling step
Compute PCA on exactly the top 500 most variable genes
Draw the Euclidean-distance heatmap with one coloring by condition and one by batch
Verify and report that each batch level contains samples of both conditions
Report the number of non-integer count entries, if any, in the step output
steps.description: Import /eval-four-models-v2-with-batch-balanced-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples; salmon gene-level counts; the record does not state whether a length correction occurred) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-batch-balanced-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows with condition and batch). Verify the 12 sample columns map 1:1 to the 12 metadata rows and that each batch level holds samples of both conditions. Check count-matrix integrality (salmon can deliver fractional values); if any entries are fractional, report the count and the largest fractional part — the DESeq2 step will round to the nearest integer and state so. Build a DESeqDataSet with the batch and condition factors, run variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design, PCA on the top 500 highly variable genes, and a heatmap of pairwise Euclidean distances, each plot colored separately by condition and by batch. Also report per-sample library sizes.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap saved, each sample distinguishable and colored by both condition and batch
Integrality of the count matrix reported (count of non-integer entries)
Any sample failing to cluster with its condition group is named explicitly

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm LFC shrinkage, batch in design
caveats: Length offset is lost (salmon gene table, no transcript-level or length input): state in the report that changes in isoform use can appear as differential expression
Do not apply ComBat-seq or any pre-test batch adjustment; the design term handles the balanced batch. Harmony is a single-cell method and must not be used on this bulk design
With 6 replicates per group DESeq2 sets the p-value to NA for Cook's-distance-flagged genes instead of replacing counts; inspect the counts of any flagged gene that lands in the result set
If fractional counts had to be rounded, state the rounding in the step output and the report
steps.context: Counts are a salmon gene-level table delivered as counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples); the import state (whether a length correction occurred) is not established in the record. Per the governing rule the model is fitted on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and the limitation — that a change in isoform use can show up as differential expression — is carried into the report. Batch: two known processing batches, each holding both conditions (balanced), from metadata.csv.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples after accounting for the two balanced processing batches, using the DESeq2 Wald test?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm LFC shrinkage per R-0029@22ca; balanced batch as a design term per R-0006@c407; salmon gene table with unestablished import state fitted without length offset per R-0169@18ab

constraints: Fit the model on the counts as delivered with no length offset; do not run tximport on this gene table and do not invent a transcript-length input
Do not scale, transform, or normalize the counts before the model; the median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq are the normalization
Pre-filter only: keep genes with >= 10 counts in at least 6 samples; keep independent filtering ON in results()
Set the condition reference level explicitly to 'control' by an explicit factor call; name the contrast (condition, treated, control)
Design formula must be ~ batch + condition; the batch is a design term, not a pre-adjustment
Shrink the reported LFC with apeglm on the single contrast coefficient; keep the unshrunken estimate beside it
Select genes by BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05 only; do not select by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone
Report the count of genes with NA p-value from Cook's-distance outlier flagging, separately from the count removed by independent filtering
steps.description: Fit the primary differential expression model. Use the integer count matrix established in T1S1 (rounding any fractional salmon entries to the nearest integer and stating so — do not invent a length input). Keep genes with >= 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size); leave the independent filtering of results() on. Set the condition reference level explicitly to 'control' (verify the actual level strings in metadata.csv first) and name the contrast as factor=condition, numerator=treated, denominator=control, so a positive log2 fold change means higher expression in treated. Design formula ~ batch + condition: the balanced batch enters as a fixed-effect covariate; no counts are adjusted before the model. DESeq() estimates median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative binomial model — do not pre-normalize, scale, or transform. Run the Wald test via results() at alpha 0.05; shrink the reported log fold change with apeglm (single coefficient, so apeglm applies, not ashr); keep the unshrunken estimate, its standard error, and the test p-values in the table. Record the number of genes whose p-value is NA from Cook's-distance outlier flagging (with 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags and sets NA rather than replacing), reported separately from genes removed by independent filtering, and the number of genes filtered pre-model. Plot the unadjusted p-value histogram before trusting the adjustment. No fold-change threshold was stated in the question, so no lfcThreshold is applied; selection is by adjusted p-value < 0.05 only. Save the full result table with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange.
acceptance_criteria: Full result table saved for every tested gene: baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and apeglm shrunken log2FoldChange
Number of genes with padj < 0.05 reported
Count of NA-pvalue genes from outlier flagging and count of independently-filtered genes both reported
Design formula, explicit reference level, and named contrast recorded in the step output

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test, same batch-aware design (second method)
caveats: Do not reuse DESeq2 size factors; TMM is the edgeR scaling
steps.context: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the sanctioned second method for this replicate count (2-11 per group), and the overlap of the two methods is what the report step must present. Input is the same 12,000 x 12 count matrix and metadata (condition, batch) as T1S2.
steps.question: With the same ~ batch + condition design, which genes does the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test call different between treated and control — the second method whose overlap with DESeq2 defines the high-confidence set?

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method per R-0001@9a17, whose overlap the report must state per R-0042@54e1, on the same balanced-batch design term per R-0006@c407

constraints: Use the same integer count matrix and the same design ~ batch + condition as T1S2
Run filterByExpr with the full design (batch + condition) before the model and report the gene count after filtering
Normalize with TMM scaling factors; do not apply batch-adjusted counts to the test
Set the condition reference level to 'control' and test the treated-vs-control contrast
Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 and report the number of genes with FDR < 0.05
steps.description: Run the robustness method on the identical integer count matrix and the identical design. Apply filterByExpr with the full design (batch + condition) before modeling, so genes uninformative for either factor are dropped; report the number of genes remaining. Estimate TMM scaling factors, fit glmQLFit with design ~ batch + condition (condition reference level 'control'), and run glmQLFTest on the treated-vs-control contrast. Adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 and save the full table (logFC, p, FDR per gene). Do not give the test batch-adjusted counts.
acceptance_criteria: Full edgeR QL result table (logFC, p, FDR) saved for all tested genes
Number of genes after filterByExpr reported
Number of genes with FDR < 0.05 reported

steps.name: Report: diagnostics, gene table, two-method overlap, reproducibility record
caveats: Disagreement between the two methods at low counts is expected; keep such genes out of the high-confidence set
steps.context: Inputs: result tables and plots from T1S2 (DESeq2 + apeglm) and T1S3 (edgeR QL), QC plots from T1S1, plus the original counts.csv and metadata.csv paths for the record. No reference data needed.
steps.question: What is the high-confidence set of genes that differ between treated and control (the DESeq2/edgeR intersection), and what does the complete, reproducible report contain?

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step; it follows the cited claims (shrunken/unshrunken LFC columns, MA and dispersion diagnostics, two-method overlap, report fields, reproducibility record)

constraints: Report the intersection of the two methods' significant gene sets as the high-confidence set; list genes called by only one method as a secondary set named by that method; do not present the union as the result
Gene table must carry both the unshrunken log2FoldChange and the shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm) with lfcSE; rank genes and plots on the shrunken value
Place the MA plot and the dispersion plot before the gene tables and state what each shows
State the lost length offset explicitly (salmon gene table, no transcript-level input)
Include the full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, design, contrast, thresholds, seed, n_tested, n_DE
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1-T1S3 outputs. Include: the sample-structure PCA and distance heatmap (colored by condition and batch) with the statement on where batch sits relative to condition; the MA plot and the dispersion plot (the two fit diagnostics), with each labeled; the unadjusted p-value histogram and a one-line reading of its shape; the gene table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, and padj, ranked by the shrunken LFC; per-method counts of genes tested and DE at adjusted p-value < 0.05; the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set with the method-specific-only genes listed as a secondary set named by method — never the union; the count of NA-pvalue genes from Cook's-distance flagging; the count of pre-filtered and independently filtered genes; and the statement that the salmon length offset was not established and is lost, so changes in isoform use can appear as differential expression. The reproducibility record must carry sessionInfo with all package versions, the random seed(s) used, the design formula and contrast, the thresholds (adjusted p-value 0.05, no fold-change threshold applied), n_tested, n_DE, and the data file names.
acceptance_criteria: Report file contains MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, and the QC plots with batch/condition colorings
Gene table saved and ranked by shrunken LFC with unshrunken LFC and lfcSE columns present
Per-method n_tested and n_DE stated, and the DESeq2/edgeR intersection and the method-specific secondary sets listed
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, versions, design, thresholds, seed) present in the report

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE, batch-aware
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is human kidney bulk RNA-seq: a salmon gene-level count table (12,000 genes x 12 samples) with a sample metadata table holding condition (treated/control, 6+6) and two known processing batches, balanced across conditions. The question is a plain treated-vs-control differential expression with a batch covariate. Per the Inflexa procedure for this situation: (1) blind-VST sample structure QC before any test, colored by condition and batch, since batch balance must be visually confirmed and any outlier sample would bias a two-group test; (2) DESeq2 Wald test on the counts as delivered — the record does not establish that a salmon length correction occurred, so no length offset is applied and no tximport is run on the gene table (stated as a limitation, not a fix) — with the batch as a fixed-effect design term (~ batch + condition), explicit control reference, minimal pre-filter (10 counts in >= 6 samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, apeglm LFC shrinkage, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on; (3) the same design under edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method, so the report can state the intersection as the high-confidence set; (4) a report carrying the two fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, per-method tested/DE counts, the two-method overlap, and a full reproducibility record. Resources are sized for a 12,000 x 12 count matrix — small by bulk-seq standards.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >= 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ batch + condition with explicit reference level
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm
Benjamini-Hochberg with DESeq2 independent filtering, alpha 0.05
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
DE report: MA and dispersion plots, gene table with unshrunken and shrunken LFC, two-method overlap, reproducibility record

DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm
Benjamini-Hochberg with DESeq2 independent filtering, alpha 0.05
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
DE report: MA and dispersion plots, gene table with unshrunken and shrunken LFC, two-method overlap, reproducibility record

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >= 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ batch + condition with explicit reference level
DESeq2 Wald test
